A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GCE-Pose and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. v2 includes supplementary material absent from the supplied v1, which ends after the references. All supplied material supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCE-Pose evaluations on HouseCat6D and NOCS-REAL275 in Table 1, alongside original ablations in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original reconstruction, sensitivity, symmetry and baseline-comparison results in supplementary Tables 4–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the keypoint extraction, two-stage semantic shape reconstruction, global-context fusion, pose estimator and losses. The supplement supplies implementation details without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HouseCat6D and NOCS-REAL275. Added analyses reuse their existing categories and the reconstruction and pose outputs already studied; no additional dataset, domain or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: Supplementary Table 8 adds Self-DPDN to the HouseCat6D comparison. v1 lacked this comparator on HouseCat6D, although its NOCS-REAL275 comparison already included DPDN. Comparator membership in the retained main tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The supplement adds reconstruction evaluation using Chamfer distance against CAD-sampled ground truth in NOCS space. Table 5 introduces controlled variations in keypoint count and loss weights. Existing benchmark splits, pose metrics and stated training settings are retained; newly documented default settings do not establish experimental changes.

E4.justification: The supplement substantially broadens diagnostics beyond the original prior and fusion ablations: quantitative reconstruction assessment, keypoint/loss-weight sensitivity, a symmetric-glass key-versus-value analysis, keypoint NOCS-error comparisons, and further semantic-consistency visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their values, but supplementary Tables 4–8 add substantial results, including mean reconstruction Chamfer distance of 2.39 × 10^-3 and glass-category 5°2cm scores of 59.16 versus 64.86 for value versus key features. Expanded Table 7 reports geometry-only/semantics-only scores of 22.73/22.16, conflicting with 22.2/22.7 in retained Table 2 without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20 retain equivalent mathematical content. Supplementary Equation 21 spells out standard Chamfer distance for reconstruction evaluation; no substantive changes to the mathematical model, assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same SSR/GCE framework, performance claims on the two benchmarks, and robustness claims concerning occlusion and intra-class shape variation.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 3 adds a symmetry-specific explanation: positional information makes key features distinguishable around rotationally symmetric regions where value features remain ambiguous. The existing limitation concerning category-specific semantics and instance-level alignment is retained.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 1 supplies substantial missing reproduction details: the DINOv2 variant, prototype initialization and curriculum, 1000/30-epoch SSR stages, augmentation, loss weights, learning rates, eight-camera rendering, 200-neighbor aggregation, and dataset-specific segmentation-mask sources. These are newly disclosed details rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Arthur and Vassilvitskii's K-means++ for initialization and Huang et al.'s SSR-2D in the semantic/geometric context discussion. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main sections and prose remain largely unchanged. v2 adds an organized four-section supplement and makes limited terminology and capitalization edits, without substantially rewriting or reorganizing the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Existing diagrams are restyled, and Figure 4 changes a displayed example and zoomed insets. Added Tables 4–8 and Figures 6–11 substantially extend the presentation with PCA feature displays, error overlays, multi-scene image grids, semantic-transfer panels and expanded ablation tables.

improvement.justification: The supplement improves reproducibility and adds useful reconstruction, sensitivity and symmetry evidence. These gains are tempered by unexplained inconsistencies: Table 7 reverses the geometry/semantics ablation ranking in Table 2 and reports AG-Pose(DINO) IoU75 as 56.07 versus 53.0 in Table 1. The documentation gain is clear, but confidence in the expanded ablation evidence is limited.
